Hemlock Valley is not in Mission: it is unincorporated land in Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area C, governed by the FVRD's Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (November 2019), even though listings carry Mission or Agassiz mailing addresses.

The plan area is based on the Controlled Recreation Area (CRA) the Province established in 2016 with approval of the Hemlock Valley All Seasons Resort Master Plan, for what is now Sasquatch Mountain Resort.
The village streets named in the plan area include Sakwi Creek Road, Edelweiss Drive, Mt Downing Road, Enzian Way and Snowflake Crescent, and the resort's own address is 20955 Hemlock Valley Road.

Per the OCP, the largest nearby town is Agassiz in the District of Kent, approximately 38 kilometres away; Mission is approximately 55 kilometres west, and the Village of Harrison Hot Springs sits south of the plan area.

Inside the plan area, the OCP names three planning neighbourhoods — Hemlock West (the historic resort community), Hemlock East and Hemlock North — each to be detailed through neighbourhood plans as the resort expands.

The village is small: the FVRD's Hemlock Valley Evacuation Guide describes approximately 200 dwellings, mainly vacation homes and short-term rentals, with Sasquatch Mountain Resort at the village's upper end. Evacuation Guide - Hemlock Valley.pdf

The existing resort accommodation base recorded in the OCP is 226 resort residential units equating to 1,072 bed units, about 60 percent of them ski-in/ski-out or within comfortable walking distance of the base area.
Forms in the village are detached cabins and chalets on the named streets, half-duplex product on Snowflake Crescent, and slope-side condo units at 21000 Enzian Way.
The community has an organised owner body: the Hemlock Valley Homeowners Association, established in 1980, is a non-profit that works on behalf of valley homeowners.

blocks.text: Hemlock Valley: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The OCP's Development Permit Areas, in its Schedule I, include protection of development from hazardous conditions, so a slope lot can need a development permit from the FVRD before building.

The OCP's build-out distribution proposes 40 percent public (nightly-rental) bed units, 45 percent private bed units and 15 percent resident/employee deed-restricted housing at full build-out — a plan target, not a description of today's tenure.

The resort expansion in the provincially approved Resort Master Plan is a phased build-out toward 19,969 bed units and a Balanced Resort Capacity of 16,641 visitors per day — a long-range plan vision longer than the life of the plan, not built product.

blocks.text: Hemlock Valley: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: There is no public transit to Hemlock Valley: the FVRD administers three BC Transit routes — Route 66 Fraser Valley Express, Route 71 Agassiz-Harrison and Route 72 Hope — and none is routed to the valley.
The FVRD publishes a Hemlock Valley Evacuation Guide, and its evacuation route runs past Sts'ailes First Nation and Harrison Mills — the valley has one road out. Evacuation Guide - Hemlock Valley.pdf

The FVRD's Electoral Area C 2026 residential utility rate sheet lists water systems for Morris Valley and Lake Errock and a Morris Valley sewer system; no Hemlock Valley system appears on it, so valley water and sewer servicing is a parcel-level question, not an FVRD utility bill lookup. Area C - Residential Rates 2026.pdf
The resort is smoke-free: Sasquatch Mountain Resort states it is completely smoke-free, including vaping, across all resort areas.
The Hemlock Valley Homeowners Association has represented valley owners since 1980 and is the community body a new owner will meet first.
Mailing addresses mislead: a Hemlock Valley property can carry a Mission or an Agassiz postal address (V0M 1A1) while sitting in neither municipality.

blocks.text: Hemlock Valley: development and new projects

items.t: Hemlock Valley All Seasons Resort build-out, under the provincially approved Resort Master Plan and the FVRD OCP: a phased expansion from the existing 226 resort residential units (1,072 bed units) toward 19,969 bed units at full build-out, with Hemlock East and Hemlock North to be detailed through neighbourhood plans as the resort expands. Status: long-range approved plan vision, not a construction schedule; no phase timing is stated in the OCP (as of November 3, 2026).

The Speculation and Vacancy Tax does not apply here: the Province's taxable-areas list names municipalities only — the City of Abbotsford, the City of Chilliwack and the District of Mission are listed, and unincorporated FVRD Electoral Area C is not a taxable area.
Area C - Residential Rates 2026.pdf

Driving is the only way in or out: the valley is reached by road from the Agassiz / Harrison Mills side, and the FVRD evacuation route runs past Sts'ailes First Nation and Harrison Mills. Evacuation Guide - Hemlock Valley.pdf
The resort's own site describes Sasquatch Mountain Resort as "just 2 hours from Vancouver" — the operator's description, not a measured time.
The nearest towns for services are Agassiz, approximately 38 kilometres away per the OCP, and Mission, approximately 55 kilometres west.

blocks.text: Hemlock Valley: risks and due diligence

items.t: Wildfire interface is a named hazard layer here: the OCP carries a Hazard and Risk Management chapter including a Wildfire Interface Hazard section, and the valley sits in forested mountain terrain.
Check the lot's Development Permit Area status with the FVRD before valuing a slope lot: the OCP's Schedule I Development Permit Areas include protection of development from hazardous conditions.
Evacuation is a real due-diligence item, not a formality: the FVRD publishes a valley-specific evacuation guide with a single route out past Harrison Mills. Evacuation Guide - Hemlock Valley.pdf

Servicing must be confirmed parcel by parcel: the OCP's infrastructure chapter covers water supply, sanitary sewer, stormwater, snow clearing and solid waste for the plan area, but which system a given lot is on, and its fees, are not published in the plan.

faq.q: Is Hemlock Valley part of Mission?
faq.a: No. It is unincorporated Fraser Valley Regional District Electoral Area C land governed by the FVRD's Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan. Real estate reporting groups a "Hemlock" sub-area under the community Mission, and listings carry Mission or Agassiz mailing addresses, but neither city governs the valley: permits, zoning and taxes run through the FVRD and the Province.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to?
faq.a: The Province, not a city and not the FVRD. A property outside any municipality is in a rural area: its owner receives the tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays the Province.

faq.q: Where do children go to school?
faq.a: There is no school in the valley. The OCP states the small permanent population will limit the viability of locating schools and medical services inside the Controlled Recreation Area, so students travel to outside communities.

faq.q: What is the ski hill, in the plan's own numbers?
faq.a: Sasquatch Mountain Resort, recorded in the OCP as 4 ski lifts servicing 146.8 hectares of developed ski terrain on 35 named trails, on the south and southwest slopes, using a 100 percent natural snowpack, with a Comfortable Carrying Capacity of about 1,150 skiers and boarders per day. The resort's own site describes it as 100 percent Canadian owned and completely smoke-free across all resort areas.
